articles.title: Core Web Vitals Field Data Measures What Real Visitors Experience
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Core Web Vitals are a set of three page-experience metrics that Google reports from real Chrome usage, and they describe how visitors actually experience loading, interactivity and visual stabil…
articles.body: TL;DR Core Web Vitals are a set of three page-experience metrics that Google reports from real Chrome usage, and they describe how visitors actually experience loading, interactivity and visual stability. The three metrics answer three different questions about one visit: Largest Contentful Paint for loading, Interaction to Next Paint for interactivity and Cumulative Layout Shift for visual stability. A page is judged on the 75th percentile of page loads, segmented across mobile and desktop, so the reported number describes nearly every visit and leaves the slowest tail out of the verdict. INP measures every click, tap and keyboard interaction a visitor makes, reports the longest one, drops one highest interaction for every 50, then takes the 75th percentile of page views.

The 191-foot-tall (58 meters) rocket was transferred 0.93 miles (1.5 kilometers) from a vertical integration building to the pad over the course of around two hours, starting around 4 a.m. EST (0900 GMT, or 5 p.m. Beijing Time), according to China Central Television (CCTV). articles.title: n8n Filter Node: Six Leases In, Three Out. Open the Discarded Pile Before You Trust It (Then Clean Up With Edit Fields)
articles.excerpt: Most office lists are mostly noise. Forty rows, and six need something done today. In n8n the step that finds those six is the Filter node, and the step that turns each one into something readable is…
articles.body: Most office lists are mostly noise. Forty rows, and six need something done today. In n8n the step that finds those six is the Filter node, and the step that turns each one into something readable is Edit Fields (Set) . Together they shorten a list with no code. This walkthrough uses a made-up property management office that needs to send renewal offers before leases run out. Manual trigger → Sample leases → Filter → Edit Fields (Set) The sample data lives inside the workflow, so you can rebuild it with no accounts connected. In a real office the second node would be Google Sheets or Airtable, and an email or Slack step would follow. The middle two nodes stay the same.

articles.title: The Java4Shell fix lives in the fourth version number
articles.excerpt: My laptop has two JDKs on Oracle's list of builds hit by Java4Shell: 27.0.1.0.3 and 21.0.13.0.3. Neither one can be hit. The builds that fix it are 27.0.1.1 and 21.0.13.1. Read those twice. The differ…
articles.body: My laptop has two JDKs on Oracle's list of builds hit by Java4Shell: 27.0.1.0.3 and 21.0.13.0.3. Neither one can be hit. The builds that fix it are 27.0.1.1 and 21.0.13.1. Read those twice. The difference is one digit, in a slot a lot of version checks throw away. Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) went public on Tuesday from the security shop Calif, and it climbed to 623 points on Hacker News . It's a heap overwrite in HotSpot's hand-written AVX-512 Base64 decoder. Once the JIT has compiled the fast path, 64 A characters and one = make the stub compute a negative output length, store a full 64-byte vector anyway, and land 62 bytes past the end of a 50-byte array.

articles.body: OpenSparrow v4.7 brings a light / dark / system theme, a "My history" panel with your recent record clicks, a Files tab that only appears where it makes sense, and nine new languages (29 in total) — one upgrade, no migration. A theme that follows you The avatar menu now carries a Theme button cycling Light → Dark → System. The choice is remembered per browser, and System tracks your OS setting live — flip the device to dark and the app follows without a reload. A tiny bootstrap script applies the theme before the stylesheet loads, so dark-mode users no longer start every page with a white flash. Under the hood it is one set of design tokens: dark mode simply redefines the same CSS variables, so every screen — grid, board, calendar, forms — adapts automatically.

articles.title: How we turned 95 different status pages into one data model
articles.excerpt: When a deploy fails, how long does it take you to figure out if the problem is with your code or with GitHub, Cloudflare, or OpenAI? For us, it usually took about 20 minutes to check each status page…
articles.body: When a deploy fails, how long does it take you to figure out if the problem is with your code or with GitHub, Cloudflare, or OpenAI? For us, it usually took about 20 minutes to check each status page one at a time. That’s why Matias and I built StatusPane. It tracks the official status pages of 95 services and puts them all together on one page. You can choose just the components you use, group them by app, and get an email or webhook when something changes. You can also see the live status of everything, no sign-up required: https://statuspane.io/status StatusPane is in beta and free to use. If your product relies on third-party APIs, I’d love your feedback. Which services should we add, and how would you like to get alerts? This is mine and Matias Leidemer side project.

articles.body: The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

articles.title: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
articles.excerpt: Open data from NASA’s Fermi mission helped an international team of scientists develop a method for finding pulsars about a million times faster than before.
articles.body: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters.
